what_this_file_is: Six questions a payment dispute would ask, answered against what this repository can actually produce, with the file that proves each answer. It is machine-read by tools/settlement_boundary.py, which refuses an answer of 'supported' that points at a missing file and refuses the two facts below being anything but false.

questions.question: Did someone run this verifier against these exact bytes?
questions.proves: A receipt records verifier version, corpus digest, per-case table, the command and a named runner; tools/check_outward_receipt.py refuses one that omits any of them.

questions.question: Were these bytes unchanged since a date anyone can check?
questions.proves: A digest list can be signed with Ed25519 and timestamped by an independent TSA, verified offline; ANCHORS.json records one state per output.
questions.limit: Implemented and measured locally; not yet exercised on a published release. No OpenTimestamps proof is shipped while the client is absent - the report says 'unavailable' rather than implying an anchor.

questions.question: Was the party who ran it authorised to act for the party they named?
questions.proves: A one-hop, time-boxed delegation record pinned to the corpus digest, with the proposer unable to be the decider.
questions.limit: One signature, not a threshold; no revocation registry; the identity is bound only when the delegator's key is supplied out of band, and the checker says 'identity unbound' otherwise.

questions.question: Was the charge inside the mandate's amount, merchant and currency limits?
questions.limit: This format binds an action to evidence bytes; it carries no mandate, no amount, no merchant and no currency. A corpus that judges exactly that exists elsewhere - probityai's vectors-agent-payment-mandate, 15 cases over 11 rules - and our answer to it is that it is theirs, not ours.

questions.question: Who bears the loss if the charge was not authorised?
questions.limit: No field in this format, and no sentence in this repository, allocates liability. Saying otherwise would be a legal claim dressed as a technical one.

questions.question: Can this be filed with an acquirer or arbitrator as evidence?
questions.limit: Admissibility is decided by the forum, under its rules, by people who are not us. This repository can make a record replayable; it cannot make a record admissible.

how_to_reproduce: python tools/settlement_boundary.py; it exits 1 if any document scanned for payment claims contains one of the banned phrases, and 3 if a 'supported' answer points at a file that is not in the repository.
